- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for the next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20), model often overpredicts downward moves; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overreacts and overshoots; reduce forecast by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 10–15 days of price action shows strong mean reversion, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture rebound.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.15+), model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture continuation; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 5–7 days.
